implementation.scope: shared render-only live-water presentation on all runnable rivers
implementation.former_dominant_band: 0.115 m sinusoid with phase 0.19 * station + 0.61 * lateral
implementation.replacement: two calm phase-warped ripples plus four hydraulically activated incommensurate, phase-warped crest bands with a smooth reach-scale energy packet
implementation.crest_alignment: primary and secondary phases are station-dominant so crests remain approximately cross-channel rather than forming one bank-to-bank diagonal ramp
implementation.phase_and_envelope_derivatives: analytical station and lateral derivatives feed the presentation normal

p2_contracts: no repeat at the former dominant 33.07 m wavelength

p4_all_river_map_loads.known_environment_warning: offline generate_204 timeout while loading Zambezi

visual_evidence.method: Separate deterministic five-second 1280x720 Metal captures at scalability 2 use the identical saved map and fixed camera. Image metrics are descriptive and are not photoreal acceptance thresholds.
visual_evidence.finding: The former continuous analytical diagonal band is removed and the center water now breaks into shorter, lower phase-warped crests. The large right-edge rise remains because it is present in the sampled surface and bounded hydraulic-relief term; this milestone intentionally does not flatten solver-authored geometry. Water still lacks a convincing high-resolution aerated hole, recirculating body, spray, and measured seasonal behavior, so photoreal acceptance remains open.

remaining_photoreal_defects: The retained sampled hydraulic rise is still broad and smooth because the source field and bathymetry are low resolution and procedural rather than seasonally measured Zambezi data.
The strongest rapid does not yet present a convincing aerated hole, recirculating entrained-air volume, converging tongues, or collision-aware spray and mist.
The phase-warped displacement is a deterministic presentation layer, not a validated free-surface hydraulic simulation.
The 30 m source terrain, synthetic ground cover, hard waterline transitions, and sparse near-field geology remain visibly procedural.
Raft, equipment, character animation, paddle contact, and final foam occlusion still require named lifelike art acceptance.
A target-hardware GPU profile and named multi-discipline art review have not accepted the combined terrain, water, VFX, raft, and crew presentation.
required_external_acceptance_gates: local Zambezi guide approval of rapid stations, lines, portages, access, hazards, rescue routes, and seasonal behavior
geospatial approval of centerline, horizontal and vertical datums, high-resolution terrain, bank breaklines, rapid rocks, and bathymetry
rights and distribution approval for the supplied map PDF, height image, reference imagery, and production derivatives
seasonal-flow and rapid-specific hydraulic validation against observed Zambezi behavior
southern African gorge geology, ecology, and environment-art approval
named photoreal water-VFX, raft, equipment, character, animation, and occlusion approval
desktop and VR target-hardware performance, collision, capsize, recovery, and complete-run gameplay acceptance
